source_a.rule: Unless an approved exception applies, students must maintain 75% attendance in a course to be eligible for its semester examination.

source_b.rule: Approved medical circumstances may be considered when evaluating a student's attendance record, but approval does not automatically guarantee examination eligibility.

source_c.rule: Students with an approved medical circumstance may be eligible with minimum attendance of 65%.

explanation: The general examination eligibility rule establishes a 75% attendance requirement, while the structured medical exception permits examination eligibility at 65% for approved medical circumstances. The corpus does not clearly establish which provision takes precedence.

source_a.rule: Unless an approved exception applies, students must maintain 75% attendance in a course to be eligible for its semester examination.

source_b.rule: Students representing the university in an officially authorized activity may request attendance consideration for the period of the authorized activity.

source_c.rule: Students with an approved university-authorized activity may be eligible with minimum attendance of 70%.

explanation: The general examination rule requires 75% attendance unless an approved exception applies, while the structured exception table specifies 70% for officially authorized university activities. The corpus does not provide sufficiently explicit precedence language resolving the two requirements.

source_a.rule: A student arriving more than 30 minutes after the scheduled examination start time will normally not be permitted to enter the examination room.

source_b.rule: A student attending a special examination session may be permitted to enter up to 45 minutes after the scheduled start time.

source_c.rule: A student experiencing an emergency delay may be considered for admission up to 45 minutes after the scheduled start time.

explanation: The general examination rule establishes a 30-minute late-entry boundary, while the examination rules table introduces special and emergency circumstances allowing consideration up to 45 minutes. The correct outcome depends on whether the special condition applies.
